rawContent: @KZiwica @nareenyoung What I do find particularly compelling about this latest round of #MeToo is not just that countless women were traumatised and stymied in their careers, but also that it exposes the horrifically vintage attitudes & behaviours of judges that are ruling on DFV & sex assault cases

@KZiwica @nareenyoung I think that's why it resonates so strongly. Yes, also because the victims are privileged and 'powerful' in their own rights, but also because it has far larger ripple effects on the culture. Same for Hollywood #MeToo. They are the culture-makers - they have enormous influence.

When #MeToo hit Hollywood first, and now the judicial system, it didn't just prioritise privileged victims. It went for two of the most influential parts of our culture: one that establishes dominant cultural narratives, & the other that decides what is socially permissible.

That's why we need to look at how #MeToo doesn't just seek justice for the women directly affected by the predatory workplace behaviour, but how exposing that predatory behaviour actually may change culture, the law etc.
@Jess_campaigns Exactly. The macro impacts often get left out of #MeToo analysis
